claims.text: The funding is for individuals from low-income households.
The funding is to cover the cost of tuition fees for undergraduate studies.
The maximum award amount is £1,820 per year for a full-time degree course.
Applications are open from June 1, 2026, to December 1, 2026.
Applicants must demonstrate that their financial circumstances do not allow them to cover tuition fees.
Retrospective applications will not be accepted.
Applicants must live in a low-income household.

Applicants must be ordinarily resident in Scotland and have completed at least two full years of secondary schooling or college education in Scotland, or demonstrate a substantial and recent connection to Scotland.
Applicants must be entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK, have Limited Leave to Remain valid for the entire course duration, or be an asylum seeker.
Applicants must not be eligible for public funds (e.g., grants or loans) towards tuition fees.
Applicants must not have already graduated with a university degree, though exceptions may be considered for a second undergraduate degree.

Applicants must have an unconditional offer for, or be a continuing student on, an undergraduate degree course at a Scottish Institute of Higher Education or a course validated by a Scottish university but delivered elsewhere in Scotland.
HNC, HND, Access courses, Accelerated degree courses with graduate entry, courses outside Scotland, Open University courses, CPD courses, and university courses below degree level are not eligible.
The fund has a budget to support students who completed an undergraduate degree in the past and wish to start a new undergraduate degree in a different field of study in academic year 2026-27.
Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis.
The awards cover tuition fees only, up to a maximum of £1,820.
Household income thresholds are used as guides, not hard cut-offs, and applications are reviewed holistically.
All applications are made online.
An eligibility checker is available before applying.
Applicants will be notified of the outcome within two to three weeks if all information and references are provided promptly.
Supporting documents include proof of eligibility, university acceptance letter, SAAS Award Notice, and P60 or pay slips/Universal Credit statements.
